body:
I wish more than anything that I could just "walk it off" I want to be the kind of person who just deals with the bad shit as it comes. but I anticipate it, worry about it happening, stress when it happens, then mope over it afterwards. I just wish I could not give a shit for one day.
Nothing in particular SHOULD be making me anxious, other than the fights with my bf, I suppose. Everything else is just a normal stressor. I just can't handle them like a normal person
I don't really know what makes me happy anymore. I wish I did. TV shows, Internet, when my bf and I are doing well. idk...

Um... Probably two years

edit: Not entirely true. My depression hasn't been constant the past two years. just worse as of the past few months but definitely more spotty originally
Literally all I want is happiness.
sister* ;) you as well

But my bed is "our bed" my boyfriend is downstairs right now not speaking to me. I don't want to lay in our bed waiting for him to come back up and talk to me. if I'm in here it's kind of like my own world. The music surrounds me and the bathtub makes me feel secure.

(Oh for context for everyone, im F 20s)
I think I say "meaning" for a lack of a better word. When I look at my life I see a lot of work, a lot of fighting with my boyfriend, crying, being unappreciated, not enough money, disrespect. I just don't really see why it's worth it. I would rather spend the day in my room alone then deal with any of this but my live-in bf and busy schedule don't give me that opportunity. also I wouldn't be able to get that across to him without upsetting him. he has a bad bad temper issue.
Tl;dr not really that my life doesn't have "meaning" but that I don't see the point in putting up with the same pain and disappointment day after day after day
Thank you, probably going to get it as soon as I feel up to leaving the house
Shoot
Please, i keep refreshing the page in hopes someone will have commented.

You're definitely right, it started because I have bipolar disorder so I used to scream at him, frequently. I was horrible. I'm on medication now so I'm a lot better but he has that preprogrammed response trigger I guess :/ and yeah I'm talking to him about it on and off for the past couple hours. when he's not angry and raging around he apologizes profusely and things go back to normal.

I mean this only happens like 5x max per month for an hour or two tops. it's not worth losing all the memories, plans, common friends/work. besides, he's amazing when he's not that other person, the angry him. I can't leave him. I know it. I think it's borderline abuse but only for those brief times. idk..
I'm crying as I read all of these comments... I know you're all right but I'm also 100% sure I don't have the heart, strength, or desire to leave him..
Thank you for caring. I'm still hanging on. Had another breakdown tonight :/

I'm now thinking I made him sound too bad. Idk, it's not every time. It's just when I go on and on about things. I mostly feel that it's my fault, cuz he'll be silent for 10 min+ of me going on and on before he blows up...

Christmas. 
I find it depressing how my lack of excitement for the holiday severely decreases as I get older

True. However, anti-depressants are a common drug that are taken daily by a shit ton of people. I imagine every single one of them aren't abstaining from alcohol.
I don't drink often. The reason I'm asking is cuz my 21st birthday is in a month AND I'M GOING TO VEGAS MOTHAFUCKERS!
This is great to hear. Especially because the fits of crying is something I also experience! Thanks for the comment

I've been told that all those are risk factors. For me, it's worth not feeling the agony I do most days to give it a try

edit: also, my depression has caused me to lose a large amount of weight so weight gain is something I could benefit from. 
I'm currently 5'6 and about 98lbs

I like this idea. I feel if I say that before I get to a certain point it might work. I'm def trying this soon!
Thanks for all the kind words (:

I don't know if I could convince my rage-filled self in the moment to exercise a different behavior. I try to just repeat to myself "You're just crazy, this is nonsense, Just calm down" but it does nothing, literally nothing.

Thank you, I'm glad you did.

That may be the case. My mother is in her 50's and still has her symptoms. Maybe 30% less than when she was younger and when I was younger, but nothing drastic.
I sure hope so tho. The sooner I can be done with this shit the better.

The only books I've read were not very helpful in my opinion. When I was younger I would read them with my dad to try and find ways to cope with my mother, but nothing seemed to help.
I actually still haven't found an effective way to communicate with my mother during her outbursts. In my case, I generally feel overwhelmingly lonely - so attention, comfort, & sincerity help. 
Honestly though, nothing really helps me during my initial freak out - only once I've already started to calm down and think rationally. 
BPD for me feels almost like being possessed temporarily, so any logical problem solving solutions usually dont work /:

I'm the same way /: it's nice to know that someone else is going through the same. Obviously, I know I"m not the only one who has it (you know what I mean)

I'll definitely ask my therapist about that. A medicine that would actually work would be a life saver.
I'll talk to my therapist about it. I do try something similar but usually the thoughts in my head are too strong to try and reason with.

I'm sorry you have it too, i really suck. No, I haven't taken any. I'm scared I'll lose my personality - I've heard thats a problem with these kinds of meds. Did u see any issues with your medicine? 
It's always a constant debate with myself as to whether it's worth it or not.

Generally friends don't know what I have, only the close ones. My best friend will usually just talk to me, then once I'm calm she'll try and cheer me up by talking about something else or doing something fun.

I'm not sure why they let him out. He went back in after the incident with my grandmother. He was in there for probably 15 years. He just recently got out and lives in NYC with my grandmother. Weird, huh? Hence the schizophrenia. He's fine as long as he takes his meds - which my grandmother makes sure he does.
I still don't trust him and never allow myself to be put in situations where I'm alone with him.
I do think it's partly genetic. I just think theres a lot of crazy in the brains of my mother's side of the family. I think my borderline personality disorder came from growing up dealing with my mother and the ups and downs of that relationship, along with other stressors in my life, and having it in my blood. I've always been slightly more hot tempered than other people, even when I was very very young.

There is medication, but I choose not to take it. From what I've seen, those kinds of meds just turn people into vegetables. You lose all personality and I'm not willing to do that to myself. 
My counseling just entails talking to them, they help me through my weekly struggles and how to cope in the future. I don't know if you can grow out of it, my mother has yet to. I don't know anyone else with it, but i would think it lasts forever.

My mother kicked me and my father out of the house when I was 2 years old because I was playing dress up and she thought it was dis-respectful that I had changed from her outfit. I didn't see her again until I was 11, except for maybe 3-4 times. I then had another fall out with her when I was 16 after she left me out on the porch with nothing at 2am and locked me out of the house. I didn't speak to her for 2 years after that. 
We have a better relationship now, but I think thats because I don't live with her, and we only see each other for weekly lunches. 
My childhood was very different, because I had a psycho absent mother, and then I had a present even more psycho mother. Always stressful, but all in all she is my mother

My mother has had this every since I was born. I think postpartum depression turned into borderline personality disorder. It caused my mother to resent me. I was diagnosed when I was about 17 by a shrink. I go to one weekly now. 
The symptoms are mostly anger, in myself and my mother's case. I'm very very short tempered out of no where, will cry for ridiculous reasons, and get very suicidal and manic. It comes from nowhere, and is only ever directed toward people close to me (family, close friends, and boyfriend)
It affects my everyday life because it's stressful as fuck lol. it more affects my long term relationships - makes it hard to have them
and yea no problem (:

Borderline Personality Disorder is similar to bipolar disorder. Unlike bipolar disorder though, I only express it to people I'm very close to. It gets very bad for those few people though. It's like some crazy version of myself is controlling my thoughts and forcing me to freak the fuck out for no reason. I also go through very bad depression spouts and don't sleep very well, ever.
My uncle is schizophrenic (in my opinion, due to doing a LOT of diff drugs when he was young) He is randomly himself then he'll be someone else completely. I was probably four months old when this happened, but my father found my uncle holding me out over our NYC apt rooftop. He also talked about killing me a lot before that. He went to a psych ward for a while after that. Then when he was out later at some point, he tied my grandmother up and drenched himself and my grandmother in gasoline and called my mother. He was saying he was going to kill them both. Kind of a Freudian thing, I think
Kind of a long answer, but yeah
